messages:
anya: quick note — ran a 5k pilot comparing embed-v3 (float32) vs embed-v3-int4 on multilingual-mini dataset (en/es/pt). recall@10 dropped ~6% on short queries.

mike: oof. what's the eval run id? link to plots?

anya: run id r_2024_03_15_1. plots: https://internal/plots/r_2024_03_15_1

sasha: can you paste the table? numbers only pls

anya: 
```
model,precision,recall@1,recall@5,recall@10,median_rank
embed-v3,float32,0.58,0.75,0.82,3
embed-v3,int4,0.52,0.70,0.76,5
```

kai: interesting median_rank jump. did you use L2 norm during index build and query? we had an earlier int4 drift when normalization was applied inconsistently.

anya: yes used normalize=True for both. microbatch size 64, seed 42. index is HNSW, ef=128.

mike: can you rerun int4 with normalize=False? quick smoke to see direction.

anya: starting now. ETA ~12m. command:
```
python -m eval.run --dataset multilingual-mini --model embed-v3-int4 --normalize False --seed 42 --hnsw-ef 128
```

deploy-bot: Canary deployment 'embed-v3-int4-canary' started in region us-west-2 (pods: 3)

sasha: also check cosine vs dot. quant can change scale, so similarity metric matters.

anya: good call. adding dot/none to rerun.

eval-bot: job r_2024_03_15_1-int4-norm-false queued (priority: high)

mike: if that doesn't explain, try running with per-channel quant (int4 perchannel) vs symmetric int4.

anya: noted. will run perchannel next.

sasha: also curious if short queries (<=8 tokens) drive the drop more. can you split recall by query length?

anya: yes — single run has breakdown; short queries recall@10: float32 0.79 vs int4 0.68

kai: big gap. I bet it's alignment of projection bias on short contexts. If per-channel helps, file a model-notes ticket and tag infra for kernel selection.

anya: filing ticket: https://internal/tickets/ML-3421 "int4 shortquery recall drop - embed-v3" @sasha @mike

mike: for triage: (1) rerun with normalize False (2) eval dot product (3) per-channel int4 (4) split by query length. whoever finishes, drop results in the ticket and ping me.

anya: will update. thanks :thumbsup:

kai: fyi I'm going to queue a small CPU fallback test on dedicated infra to see if serving differences matter.

anya: cool — will include a tiny sample of failure cases in ticket (examples).

mike: sanity check — what's the training quant stat? maybe mean shift. can you run mean/std of embeddings for both precisions?

anya: ran it quickly: float32 mean L2: 1.03 std 0.12; int4 mean L2: 0.86 std 0.21

sasha: that mean shift is telling. maybe need a post-quant rescale step in the runtime. I've seen that for other models.

anya: noted. ok I'm going to let runs finish and report back here + ticket.

mike: appreciate it. let's avoid rolling int4 to prod until we have per-length parity.

anya: agreed.
